takeaways.q: At what three levels does Claude Code read CLAUDE.md?
takeaways.a: User-level (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), project-level (.claude/CLAUDE.md or root CLAUDE.md), and directory-level (subdirectory CLAUDE.md files).

takeaways.q: How are conflicting rules across multiple CLAUDE.md files handled?
takeaways.a: All discovered files are concatenated into context, not overridden. If two rules contradict, Claude may pick either — CLAUDE.md is not a hard enforcement layer.

takeaways.q: CLAUDE.md vs settings.json for must-hold rules?
takeaways.a: settings.json rules (and hooks) are enforced by the client regardless of what Claude decides. CLAUDE.md shapes behaviour but doesn't guarantee it.

takeaways.q: How does @ syntax work in CLAUDE.md?
takeaways.a: A line beginning with @ followed by a path inlines that file at load time. There is no @import keyword — just @path on its own line.

takeaways.q: What is CLAUDE.local.md?
takeaways.a: Loads after CLAUDE.md at the same level, gitignored by convention. For personal project-scoped tweaks, not team rules.

takeaways.q: What does /memory do — does it load config?
takeaways.a: It lists loaded CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.local.md files and opens them in your editor. Diagnostic only; config loads automatically by location.

takeaways.q: What survives /compact?
takeaways.a: Project-root CLAUDE.md is re-read from disk after compaction. Nested and path-scoped files load on demand and return when Claude next reads a matching file.

takeaways.q: New team member gets inconsistent Claude Code behaviour on the same repo/branch. Most common root cause?
takeaways.a: Conventions live in the existing dev's user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, which isn't version-controlled or shared. Move them to project level.

takeaways.q: Directory-level CLAUDE.md vs .claude/rules/ with paths?
takeaways.a: Directory CLAUDE.md covers one directory. For conventions spanning many directories, use .claude/rules/ with glob patterns in YAML frontmatter.

traps.trap: New team member not receiving Claude Code instructions despite working on the same repo and branch
traps.why: Instructions are in user-level config (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), not shared via git. Move them to .claude/CLAUDE.md for team-wide application.

traps.trap: Thinking /memory triggers configuration loading
traps.why: /memory is diagnostic — shows which files are loaded. Config loads automatically based on location in the hierarchy.

traps.trap: Assuming directory-level CLAUDE.md is the best solution for cross-directory conventions
traps.why: Directory CLAUDE.md applies to one directory. For conventions spanning many (e.g., test files everywhere), use .claude/rules/ with glob patterns.

takeaways.q: What is a skill and how is it invoked?
takeaways.a: A named, reusable set of instructions in Markdown with optional YAML frontmatter. Invoked as a slash command (/review) or auto-loaded when a request matches its description.

takeaways.q: .claude/skills/ vs .claude/commands/ — structure?
takeaways.a: Skill = directory with SKILL.md (.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md). Command = flat file (.claude/commands/deploy.md). .claude/skills/ is canonical.

takeaways.q: Key scoping distinction in Claude Code config?
takeaways.a: Project-scoped (.claude/) = version-controlled, shared via git. User-scoped (~/.claude/) = personal, not shared. Applies to CLAUDE.md, commands/skills, and rules.

takeaways.q: When do you use context: fork in skill frontmatter?
takeaways.a: For skills producing verbose output (codebase analysis, brainstorming) — runs in an isolated sub-agent context so the main conversation stays clean.

takeaways.q: What does allowed-tools do in skill frontmatter (exam v1.0)?
takeaways.a: Restricts which tools the skill can use. (Current Claude Code pre-approves the listed tools for promptless use.)

takeaways.q: What is argument-hint?
takeaways.a: An autocomplete label showing expected arguments (e.g., [issue-number]). Makes inputs explicit without interactive prompting.

takeaways.q: Skills vs CLAUDE.md?
takeaways.a: Skills: on-demand, task-specific workflows loaded when invoked. CLAUDE.md: always-loaded universal standards with no invocation step.

takeaways.q: Personal variant of a team skill without conflicts?
takeaways.a: Create it in ~/.claude/skills/ under a different name (e.g., /deep-analyse instead of /analyse).

traps.trap: Creating a flat Markdown file directly inside .claude/skills/ (e.g., .claude/skills/review.md) and expecting a /review command
traps.why: A skill must be a directory with SKILL.md (.claude/skills/review/SKILL.md). Flat .md files create commands only under .claude/commands/.

traps.trap: Placing a team-shared command in a user-scoped path (~/.claude/commands/ or ~/.claude/skills/) instead of a project-scoped path
traps.why: User-scoped paths are personal and unshared. Team commands go in .claude/skills/ or .claude/commands/ in the repo.

traps.trap: Thinking skills behave like CLAUDE.md for always-on guidance
traps.why: Skills load on demand. For always-on conventions the answer is CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/.

traps.trap: Not knowing when to use context: fork
traps.why: Without it, verbose brainstorming/analysis output pollutes the main context window. Use it for exploratory or verbose tasks.

traps.trap: Putting task-specific workflows in CLAUDE.md
traps.why: CLAUDE.md is for always-loaded universal standards. Review workflows, analysis routines, templates → skills.

takeaways.q: How do .claude/rules/ files decide when to apply?
takeaways.a: Glob patterns in the YAML frontmatter paths field. They load only when Claude works with files matching those patterns.

takeaways.q: Why are path-scoped rules more token-efficient than root CLAUDE.md?
takeaways.a: They load only for matching files; root CLAUDE.md loads every session regardless of what you're editing.

takeaways.q: What do path rules solve that directory CLAUDE.md can't?
takeaways.a: Conventions for a file type scattered across many directories — one rule file instead of duplicates in 50+ directories.

takeaways.q: How does a glob like **/*.test.tsx provide coverage?
takeaways.a: Matches files anywhere in the codebase regardless of directory depth.

takeaways.q: Classic exam scenario for path-specific rules?
takeaways.a: Test files co-located with source across 50+ directories needing consistent conventions → .claude/rules/ with glob paths.

takeaways.q: How do you verify which path rules are loaded?
takeaways.a: /context — only rules matching the current file's path appear.

traps.trap: Choosing directory-level CLAUDE.md over path-specific rules for cross-directory conventions
traps.why: For files spread across 50+ directories, glob-scoped rules are correct; directory CLAUDE.md would need a file in every directory.

traps.trap: Placing file-type-specific conventions in root CLAUDE.md
traps.why: Root CLAUDE.md loads every session — Terraform rules eat tokens while editing React. Path rules load only for matching files.

traps.trap: Confusing skills with path-specific rules for automatic convention application
traps.why: Rules stay in context as background guidance when a matching file is read, shaping every edit. Skills load on demand as task workflows. Automatic always-on conventions for a file type → path rules.

takeaways.q: When do you choose plan mode?
takeaways.a: Complex tasks needing exploration, comparison of approaches, architectural decisions, multi-file changes, or dependency understanding before implementing.

takeaways.q: When is direct execution right?
takeaways.a: Well-scoped change, approach already known, limited to a single file/function, no design decisions.

takeaways.q: How do you enter plan mode?
takeaways.a: claude --permission-mode plan, Shift+Tab until status shows plan mode, or prefix a prompt with /plan. Writing 'plan mode' in the prompt body does nothing.

takeaways.q: What is the Explore subagent for?
takeaways.a: Isolates verbose discovery output from the main conversation, returning summaries and keeping context clean for implementation.

takeaways.q: What is the hybrid pattern?
takeaways.a: Plan-then-execute: plan mode for investigation and strategy, then direct execution to implement consistently (e.g., library migrations).

takeaways.q: What does the plan-vs-direct choice hinge on?
takeaways.a: Ambiguity, not difficulty. A hard but well-defined bug fix → direct. A simple-sounding feature with multiple approaches across modules → plan.

takeaways.q: Choose plan mode upfront, or wait for complexity to emerge?
takeaways.a: Upfront when complexity is stated in the requirements — it's known, not speculative.

traps.trap: Defaulting to direct execution for multi-file architectural changes
traps.why: Multiple valid approaches across many files need plan mode; direct execution risks costly rework.

traps.trap: Using plan mode for a single-file bug fix with a clear stack trace
traps.why: Known cause, location, and fix → direct execution. Plan mode is unnecessary overhead.

traps.trap: Not recognising the plan-then-execute hybrid pattern
traps.why: Combine plan mode for investigation with direct execution for implementation.

traps.trap: Starting direct execution and switching to plan mode only when complexity emerges
traps.why: If complexity is already stated (e.g., monolith restructuring), choose plan mode upfront.

takeaways.q: Claude Code interprets a prose description inconsistently. First technique?
takeaways.a: Give 2–3 concrete input/output examples of the exact transformation. Examples generalise more reliably than prose.

takeaways.q: Best technique for complex transformations with many edge cases?
takeaways.a: Test-driven iteration: write tests (happy path, edge cases, performance), share failures for unambiguous feedback.

takeaways.q: When do you use the interview pattern?
takeaways.a: Unfamiliar domain where you might miss considerations — have Claude ask questions before implementing to surface hidden requirements.

takeaways.q: Multiple issues that interact — how do you give feedback?
takeaways.a: All in a single message, so the model sees every constraint and produces a coherent fix.

takeaways.q: When should feedback be sequential instead?
takeaways.a: When issues are independent and don't affect each other.

takeaways.q: Interview pattern vs examples?
takeaways.a: Examples fix inconsistent interpretation when you know the exact transformation. Interview fixes missing requirements in unfamiliar domains.

takeaways.q: How many examples are enough?
takeaways.a: Two or three well-chosen ones covering the standard case and key edge cases.

traps.trap: Choosing to refine prose descriptions when the model interprets them inconsistently
traps.why: Better prose still relies on interpretation. Concrete input/output examples remove ambiguity — examples first.

traps.trap: Not recognising when to batch vs sequence feedback
traps.why: Interacting issues → one message. Independent issues → sequential.

traps.trap: Confusing the interview pattern with the examples technique
traps.why: Interview = unfamiliar domain, missing considerations. Examples = known transformation, misinterpreted. Different problems.

takeaways.q: Which flag makes Claude Code run non-interactively in CI?
takeaways.a: -p (--print): process the prompt, write to stdout, exit — no interactive input.

takeaways.q: How do you make CI output machine-parseable for PR comments?
takeaways.a: --output-format json with --json-schema; schema-validated data lands in the structured_output field of the JSON envelope.

takeaways.q: Why is review in a separate session better than self-review?
takeaways.a: The generating session keeps its reasoning context and is biased toward its own decisions. An independent instance judges on merit.

takeaways.q: How do you avoid duplicate review comments across CI runs?
takeaways.a: Include prior findings in context and instruct Claude to report only new or still-unaddressed issues.

takeaways.q: How does CLAUDE.md improve CI test generation?
takeaways.a: It documents testing standards, fixtures and review criteria; Claude reads it in CI just like interactively, so tests follow team patterns.

takeaways.q: Batch API vs real-time in CI?
takeaways.a: Real-time for blocking pre-merge checks. Batch (50% cheaper, up to 24h latency, no SLA) for non-blocking overnight/weekly analysis.

takeaways.q: --append-system-prompt vs --system-prompt?
takeaways.a: --append-system-prompt adds to the default prompt (keeps tool guidance/safety). --system-prompt replaces it entirely.

takeaways.q: How do git worktrees help parallel Claude Code sessions?
takeaways.a: Each worktree is a separate directory on its own branch — isolated edits and independent context budgets.

traps.trap: CI pipeline hanging because Claude Code is waiting for interactive input
traps.why: Use -p (--print). CLAUDE_HEADLESS=true and --batch don't exist; stdin redirection isn't the documented method.

traps.trap: Assuming self-review in the same session is as effective as independent review
traps.why: The same session retains generation reasoning and is less likely to question itself. Use an independent instance.

traps.trap: Using the Batch API for pre-merge CI checks
traps.why: Up to 24h processing, no latency SLA. Blocking checks need the real-time API; batch for overnight/weekly.

traps.trap: Not including prior review findings in subsequent review runs
traps.why: Each run starts from scratch and duplicates comments. Include prior findings; report only new/unaddressed issues.
